problem: Naively applying behaviour cloning (BC) to real-world social robot navigation yields poor policies (low success, frequent collisions), and prior IL works evaluate only in constrained scenarios with limited human interaction.
motivation: Online DRL in the wild is unsafe and needs hard-to-specify social rewards, while offline IL from safely collected expert demonstrations can be deployed zero-shot. The authors observe that BC performance depends heavily on architecture and training choices, not just data volume.
key_idea: A BC recipe (Ratatouille) combining flip data augmentation, weight perturbation, AdamW with weight decay, a hybrid discrete-continuous action-chunk head, and a reduced path-tracking embedding turns naive BC into a reliable social navigation policy without changing the data.
insight: Most gains come from training-recipe ingredients rather than data: AdamW (decoupled weight decay), weight perturbation and flip augmentation are the three most impactful ablations in both real-to-sim and sim-to-sim. Flip augmentation makes the policy robust to missing CW paths (Base drops sharply, Ratatouille does not). Action chunking and the hybrid head give modest gains, and action chunking helps little when the expert is Markovian (sim DRL expert).
method: Flip augmentation: mirror the state about the robot x-axis (negate y of robot, humans, path, and negate angular velocity), doubling data without relabelling.
Action chunking: predict H=3 future actions (inverted-U over H; H=3 best).

Hybrid action space: angular velocity discretized into 3 bins; the model outputs 3^H paths each with a probability and 2H continuous actions squashed into the bins; loss = -w_d log p_i + confidence-weighted MSE.
Weight perturbation: every 50k steps reset to the best checkpoint and move weights 30% toward a random network (w=0.7w+0.3w_rand), decaying by 0.9 every 50k steps after 750k steps.
Reduced path-tracking latent: path embedding 16-d vs human-avoidance 128-d to prevent shortcut reliance on path features.
Optimization settings: lr 1e-4, ~2M steps, larger network, AdamW with weight decay 5e-3.

Architecture/state from DRMPC: path node poses plus variable-length human/robot history (10 steps at 0.25s) with GRU/attention; single Ouster LiDAR with T&R localization, YOLOX detection and Norfair tracking.

setting.backbone: DRMPC-style GRU + multi-head attention policy network (trained from scratch with BC)
setting.training_data: 11 hours (400k steps) of real-world teleoperated demonstrations on a university campus; sim experiments use collision-free rollouts of a DRL expert (up to 500k samples)
setting.observation: single LiDAR (range + reflectivity) -> human detections/tracks (past 2.5s), robot pose and path from Teach-and-Repeat
setting.action_space: continuous unicycle linear and angular velocity (hybrid 3-bin angular + continuous chunk of H=3)
setting.simulator: Custom ORCA-based social navigation simulator from DRMPC; real-world Clearpath Jackal

numbers.eval_set_note: 24 real-world episodes (6 per path), 36 human-robot scenarios
numbers.backbone: DRMPC-style network trained with BC on 11h real data
numbers.extra: trained on real data, deployed zero-shot; baseline Base SR 0.38, CPM 0.06
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Quantitative real-world results averaged across 24 episodes

numbers.eval_set_note: 108 episodes over 27 scenarios in ORCA simulator, model trained on real data
numbers.backbone: DRMPC-style network trained with BC on 11h real data
numbers.evidence: the Base model achieves a success rate of 27.8%, while Ratatouille reaches 98.1%

numbers_note: Not a standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmark; sim ablation results (normalized reward) only in figures. Continuous ablation SR 93.5% is stated in text.
results: Ratatouille improves real-to-sim success from 27.8% to 98.1% over naive BC, and in real-world tests raises SR from 0.38 to 0.79 with CPM 0.06 to 0.01, beating SCAND (SR 0.25, CPM 0.08). Qualitative food-court deployment shows proficient behaviour with occasional collisions.
limitations: Robot observes only human positions and has perception delays, whereas the expert sees intent cues; a gap to the expert (SR 0.79 vs 1.00) remains.
Weight perturbation hypothesis (loss of plasticity in multi-objective BC) is not validated; evaluation is small (24 real episodes) with a real-to-sim gap and imbalanced data (73% path following).
